title: Participle Constructions
descriptionRussian: Причастные обороты и их место в предложении
intro: Participle constructions (причастные обороты) are participles with dependent words, functioning as extended adjectives. POSITION matters: Before noun (no commas): читающий книгу студент (the student reading a book). After noun (with commas): студент, читающий книгу, ... (the student, who is reading a book, ...). AGREEMENT: Participle agrees with the noun in gender, number, case. These constructions are common in formal/written Russian and replace который clauses for conciseness.
rules: Before noun = no commas: читающий книгу мальчик (the boy reading a book)
After noun = commas required: мальчик, читающий книгу, сидит там
Participle agrees with noun in gender, number, case
Can replace который clauses: который читает → читающий
examples: Работающие здесь люди очень добрые. (The people working here are very kind.)
Люди, работающие здесь, очень добрые. (The people, who work here, are very kind.)
Написанная им книга стала популярной. (The book written by him became popular.)
Я видел девушку, читающую книгу. (I saw a girl reading a book.)

items.prompt: _____ книгу студент сидит в библиотеке. (reading, before noun)
items.promptEnglish: The student reading a book is sitting in the library.

items.prompt: Студент, _____ книгу, сидит в библиотеке. (reading, after noun)
items.promptEnglish: The student, who is reading a book, is sitting in the library.
items.hint: After noun with commas, still nominative

items.prompt: Я видел девушку, _____ письмо. (writing, acc fem)
items.promptEnglish: I saw a girl writing a letter.

items.prompt: _____ мной книга лежит на столе. (written, before noun)
items.promptEnglish: The book written by me is on the table.

items.prompt: Мы говорили о людях, _____ в этом доме. (living)
items.promptEnglish: We talked about the people living in this house.

items.prompt: Which needs commas? _____ здесь люди / Люди _____ здесь
Я знаю человека, _____ эту статью. (who wrote)
items.promptEnglish: I know the person who wrote this article.

items.prompt: _____ на столе документы важные. (lying, before noun)
items.promptEnglish: The documents lying on the table are important.
The book written by him became a bestseller.

items.prompt: Мы встретили туристов, _____ город. (who were visiting, acc pl)
items.promptEnglish: We met tourists visiting the city.
items.hint: Agrees with туристов (m, acc animate pl)

items.prompt: _____ учителем задача была трудной. (set/assigned, before noun)
items.promptEnglish: The task set by the teacher was difficult.
items.hint: Agrees with задача (f, nom), before noun = no commas
items.explanation: Nominative feminine, before noun: поставленная учителем задача.

hints: The participle must agree in case and number with the noun it modifies. What form matches plural nominative 'студенты'?
explanations: Active past participles agree with their noun: 'студенты' is nominative plural, so the participle takes the plural nominative ending -ие: сдавшие. This replaces 'студенты, которые сдали.'
